l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: self-restraint and desires results in mockery by enemies (if one fully indulges the soul's desire)
q: If you give fully to your soul the delight of her desire, she will make you the laughing stock of your enemies.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom is known by every man of understanding
q: Every man of understanding knows wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is just (alone)
q: The Lord alone is just.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has mercy on mankind (all flesh, as a shepherd does his flock)
q: the mercy of the Lord is on all flesh: reproving, chastening, teaching, and bringing back, as a shepherd does his flock.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has mercy on chastening (those who accept it and diligently seek his judgments)
q: He has mercy on those who accept chastening, and that diligently seek after his judgments.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has works that are unfathomable (cannot be added to, taken from, or explored)
q: As for the wondrous works of the Lord, it is not possible to take from them nor add to them, neither is it possible to explore them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord multiplies forgiveness (because he sees mankind's end is evil)
q: He saw and perceived their end, that it is evil. Therefore he multiplied his forgiveness.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind has lifespan at most a hundred years
q: The number of man’s days at the most are a hundred years.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mankind is compared to a drop of water from the sea (few years in the day of eternity)
q: As a drop of water from the sea, and a pebble from the sand, so are a few years in the day of eternity.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mercy differs in scope man's mercy is on his neighbor; the Lord's is on all flesh
q: The mercy of a man is on his neighbor; but the mercy of the Lord is on all flesh

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: abomination is not wisdom (knowledge of wickedness)
q: The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: abomination is a abomination
q: There is a wickedness, and it is an abomination.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners lacks counsel (their prudence is not counsel)
q: The prudence of sinners is not counsel.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: law of the Most High belongs to the Lord (law of the Most High)
q: give place to the law of the Most High.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: deceitful man has trait inward deceit (outwardly mourning with head hung down)
q: There is one who does wickedly, who hangs down his head with mourning; but inwardly he is full of deceit,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: deceitful man has trait takes advantage of strangers (where he isn't known)
q: Where he isn’t known, he will take advantage of you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: deceitful man has trait does mischief given opportunity (restrained only by lack of power)
q: And if for lack of power he is hindered from sinning, if he finds opportunity, he will do mischief.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gossip is like arrow stuck in thigh (in a fool)
q: As an arrow that sticks in the flesh of the thigh, so is gossip in a fool.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool has trait pain over a word (travails like a woman in labor when holding gossip)
q: A fool will travail in pain with a word, as a woman in labor with a child.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool has trait lacking wisdom
q: There is a fool lacking in wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom consists of fear of the Lord
q: All wisdom is the fear of the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom includes law of the Most High (doing of the law)
q: In all wisdom is the doing of the law.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man is a person who is silent until his time has come (disposition)
q: A wise man will be silent until his time has come

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: liar has destination dishonor
q: The destination of a liar is dishonor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: liar has continual shame
q: His shame is with him continually.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: liar inherits destruction (as does a thief)
q: A thief is better than a man who is continually lying, but they both will inherit destruction.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: liar is worse than thief (continual liar)
q: A thief is better than a man who is continually lying

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speech and the tongue has effect hatred (when much talk)
q: there is one who is hated for his much talk.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speech and the tongue is worse than slip on a pavement (a slip of the tongue)
q: A slip on a pavement is better than a slip with the tongue.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gifts effect on wise blind their eyes (favors and gifts)
q: Favors and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and as a muzzle on the mouth, turn away reproofs.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gifts varies in profit (some do not profit, some repay double)
q: There is a gift that will not profit you; and there is a gift that pays back double.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man is beloved (because wise in words)
q: He who is wise in words will make himself beloved

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man advances himself (through wise words)
q: He who is wise in words will advance himself.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man pleases great men (when prudent)
q: And one who is prudent will please great men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool misses his time (braggart and fool)
q: but the braggart and fool will miss his time.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool has gift that does not profit (he expects repayment many times over)
q: The gift of a fool will not profit you, for he looks for repayment many times instead of one.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool is laughed to scorn (often, by many)
q: How often, and of how many, will he be laughed to scorn!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool has parable rejected (he does not tell it at the proper time)
q: A parable from a fool’s mouth will be rejected; for he won’t tell it at the proper time.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool has pleasantries wasted
q: but the pleasantries of fools will be wasted.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is full of compassion and mercy
q: For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who fear the Lord prepares their hearts
q: Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and will humble their souls in his sight.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who fear the Lord humbles their souls (in the Lord's sight)
q: Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and will humble their souls in his sight.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord keeps the Lord's ways
q: Those who love him will keep his ways.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who love the Lord is filled with the law
q: Those who love him will be filled with the law.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the faint-hearted and fearful is subject of woe
q: Woe to fearful hearts, to faint hands, and to the sinner who goes two ways!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the faint-hearted and fearful does not believe (therefore will not be defended)
q: Woe to the faint heart! For it doesn’t believe. Therefore it won’t be defended.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: trust in the Lord results in the Lord's help
q: Put your trust in him, and he will help you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord forgives sins
q: He forgives sins and saves in time of affliction.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: trust in the Lord results in unfailing reward (for all who fear the Lord)
q: put your trust in him, and your reward will not fail.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: divine mercy and wrath belongs to the Lord (proportional to his majesty)
q: for as his majesty is, so also is his mercy.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord saves people in time of affliction
q: He forgives sins and saves in time of affliction.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has attribute majesty matched by mercy
q: for as his majesty is, so also is his mercy.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord helps those who trust in him (condition: trust in him)
q: Put your trust in him, and he will help you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: My son is instructed to prepare soul for temptation (if he comes to serve the Lord)
q: My son, if you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for temptation.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: My son is instructed to cling to the Lord (so as to be increased at his latter end)
q: Cling to him, and don’t depart, that you may be increased at your latter end.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who fear the Lord does not disobey the Lord's words
q: Those who fear the Lord will not disobey his words.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: those who fear the Lord seeks the Lord's good pleasure
q: Those who fear the Lord will seek his good pleasure.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sin (Chapter 21) is like two-edged sword (its stroke has no healing)
q: All iniquity is as a two-edged sword. Its stroke has no healing.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sinners has way ending in Hades (way paved with stones)
q: The way of sinners is paved with stones; and at the end of it is the pit of Hades.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom is fulfilment of the Lord (fear of the Lord)
q: The fulfilment of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom is to fool like destroyed house
q: As a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool (Chapter 21) has inward parts like broken vessel (holds no knowledge)
q: The inward parts of a fool are like a broken vessel. He will hold no knowledge.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool (Chapter 21) has chatter like burden in the way
q: The chatter of a fool is like a burden in the way

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool (Chapter 21) experiences instruction as fetters on the feet
q: Instruction is as fetters on the feet of an unwise man, and as manacles on the right hand.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool (Chapter 21) lifts voice with laughter
q: A fool lifts up his voice with laughter

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool (Chapter 21) has heart located in mouth
q: The heart of fools is in their mouth

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sin (Chapter 21) is like snake (to be fled from; bites if approached)
q: Flee from sin as from the face of a snake; for if you go near, it will bite you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (Chapter 21) has knowledge like flood (counsel like a fountain of life)
q: The knowledge of a wise man will be made to abound as a flood, and his counsel as a fountain of life.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (Chapter 21) smiles quietly (clever man)
q: but a clever man smiles quietly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (Chapter 21) has mouth that is his heart
q: the mouth of wise men is their heart.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wise man (Chapter 21) has grace on lips
q: grace will be found on the lips of the wise.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: son (the speaker's son) is instructed to sin no more (and ask forgiveness for past sins)
q: My son, have you sinned? Do it no more; and ask forgiveness for your past sins.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man has supplication that reaches the Lord (reaches God's ears; judgment comes speedily)
q: Supplication from a poor man’s mouth reaches to the ears of God, and his judgment comes speedily.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: one who hates reproof is in path of sinners
q: One who hates reproof is in the path of the sinner.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is feared by wise man (Chapter 21) (he repents in his heart)
q: He who fears the Lord will repent in his heart.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slothful man is compared to defiled stone (in disgrace)
q: A slothful man is compared to a stone that is defiled.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: friend can be reconciled after drawn sword or hostile words (unless insulting, arrogance, disclosing a secret, or treacherous blow)
q: If you have opened your mouth against a friend, don’t be afraid, for there may be reconciliation, unless it is for insulting, arrogance, disclosing of a secret, or a treacherous blow— for these things any friend will flee.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: friend flees from insult, arrogance, disclosed secret, treacherous blow (any friend)
q: for these things any friend will flee.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: friendship and reconciliation is dissolved by insulting a friend
q: He who insults a friend will dissolve friendship.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: friendship and reconciliation is possible after drawing a sword against a friend (there may be a way back)
q: If you have drawn a sword against a friend, don’t despair, for there may be a way back.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slothful man is compared to filth of a dunghill
q: A slothful man is compared to the filth of a dunghill.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: slothful man receives hissing from everyone (in his disgrace)
q: Everyone will hiss at him in his disgrace.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool lacks understanding
q: Weep for a fool, for he lacks understanding.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool has life worse than death
q: the life of the fool is worse than death.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool is mourned for all the days of his life (fool and ungodly man)
q: but for a fool and an ungodly man, it lasts all the days of his life.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool is heavier than lead (named "Fool")
q: What would be heavier than lead? What is its name, but “Fool”?

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool is harder to bear than sand, salt, and iron (man without understanding)
q: Sand, salt, and a mass of iron is easier to bear than a man without understanding.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fool has madness that wearies others
q: you won’t be wearied in his madness.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speaker (author praying) addresses Lord (as Father and Master of his life)
q: O Lord, Father and Master of my life, don’t abandon me to their counsel.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: adulterous man faces punishment city streets (seized where he least expects)
q: This man will be punished in the streets of the city. He will be seized where he least expects it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord has attribute sees all ways of men (eyes ten thousand times brighter than the sun)
q: the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, seeing all the ways of men, and looking into secret places.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Lord knows all things (before creation and after completion)
q: All things were known to him before they were created, and also after they were completed.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: adulterous wife commits three offenses (against the law, her husband, and by adultery)
q: For first, she was disobedient in the law of the Most High. Second, she trespassed against her own husband. Third, she played the adulteress in fornication, and had children by another man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: adulterous wife faces punishment congregation (brought out; extends to her children)
q: She shall be brought out into the congregation. Her punishment will extend to her children.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: adulterous wife leaves a curse (her memory; reproach not blotted out)
q: She will leave her memory for a curse. Her reproach won’t be blotted out.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fear of the Lord is valued as best and sweetest (recognized by those left behind)
q: there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing sweeter than to heed the commandments of the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: speaker (author praying) asks removal of evil desire (prayer)
q: and turn away evil desire from me.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: discipline of the mouth effect on keeper not caught (for one who keeps it)
q: Listen, my children, to the discipline of the mouth. He who keeps it will not be caught.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: oaths consequence of habitual use not cleansed from sin (for one who continually utters the Name)
q: so he also who swears and continually utters the Name will not be cleansed from sin.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: oaths consequence of false swearing not justified (house filled with calamities)
q: If he has sworn falsely, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with calamities.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fornicator has disposition never ceases until fire burned out (insatiable)
q: a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease until he has burned out the fire.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fornicator finds sweet all bread (will not cease until he dies)
q: All bread is sweet to a fornicator. He will not cease until he dies.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: adulterous man believes no one sees him (thinks darkness and walls hide him)
q: A man who goes astray from his own marriage bed says in his heart, “Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and the walls hide me. No one sees me. Of whom am I afraid? The Most High will not remember my sins.”

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: adulterous man fears eyes of men (but not the Lord's eyes)
q: The eyes of men are his terror.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom originates from the Lord (came out of his mouth)
q: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a mist.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is rooted in honored people (the Lord's own inheritance portion)
q: I took root in a people that was honored, even in the portion of the Lord’s own inheritance.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is compared to trees and aromatic plants (cedar, cypress, palm, olive, plane, cinnamon, myrrh, terebinth, vine)
q: Like the terebinth, I stretched out my branches. My branches are glorious and graceful.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is exalted like tree in Lebanon (cedar)
q: I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, And like a cypress tree on the mountains of Hermon.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is exalted like tree on Hermon (cypress on the mountains)
q: I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, And like a cypress tree on the mountains of Hermon.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is exalted like plant in Jericho (rose bushes)
q: I was exalted like a palm tree on the sea shore, like rose bushes in Jericho, and like a fair olive tree in the plain.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has memory sweeter than honey (her inheritance than the honeycomb)
q: For my memory is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than the honeycomb.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is not perfectly known by first man (last man has not explored her either)
q: The first man didn’t know her perfectly. In like manner, the last has not explored her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is not explored by last man
q: The first man didn’t know her perfectly. In like manner, the last has not explored her.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has thoughts filled from sea (counsels from the great deep)
q: For her thoughts are filled from the sea, and her counsels from the great deep.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom came out as canal stream (from a river, into a garden)
q: I came out as a canal stream from a river, and as an irrigation ditch into a garden.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has throne in pillar of the cloud (lives in high places)
q: I lived in high places, and my throne is in the pillar of the cloud.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom waters garden (her stream became a river and then a sea)
q: I said, “I will water my garden, and will drench my garden bed.” Behold, my stream became a river, and my river became a sea.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom labors for those who seek wisdom (not for herself only)
q: See that I have not labored for myself only, but for all those who diligently seek wisdom.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: book of the covenant is identified with Wisdom (all these things)
q: All these things are the book of the covenant of the Most High God, the law which Moses commanded us for an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: book of the covenant belongs to the Lord (covenant of the Most High God)
q: All these things are the book of the covenant of the Most High God, the law which Moses commanded us for an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: book of the covenant commanded by Moses (the law)
q: the law which Moses commanded us for an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: book of the covenant is inheritance for Jacob (assemblies of Jacob)
q: the law which Moses commanded us for an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord makes abundant Wisdom (like Pishon and Tigris in first fruits)
q: It is he who makes wisdom abundant, as Pishon, and as Tigris in the days of first fruits.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord makes full Euphrates (understanding full as the Euphrates and Jordan)
q: He makes understanding full as the Euphrates, and as the Jordan in the days of harvest,

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord makes shine Gihon (instruction shines as light, as Gihon in vintage)
q: who makes instruction shine forth as the light, as Gihon in the days of vintage.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom created by the Lord (created from the beginning, before the ages)
q: He created me from the beginning, before the ages.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has duration eternal (will not cease to exist for all ages)
q: For all ages, I will not cease to exist.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom dwells in Jacob (dwelling assigned by the Creator)
q: ‘Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Israel.’

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has inheritance in Israel (assigned by the Creator)
q: ‘Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Israel.’

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom is established in Zion (after ministering in the holy tabernacle)
q: In the holy tabernacle, I ministered before him. So I was established in Zion.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom ministers in holy tabernacle (before the Most High)
q: In the holy tabernacle, I ministered before him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: Wisdom has domain in Jerusalem (given rest in the beloved city)
q: In the beloved city, likewise he gave me rest. In Jerusalem was my domain.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman changes her appearance (darkens her countenance like a bear)
q: The wickedness of a woman changes her appearance, and darkens her countenance like that of a bear.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fear of the Lord is glory of elderly people
q: Much experience is the crown of the aged. Their glory is the fear of the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wisdom is beautiful in elderly people
q: How beautiful is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men who are in honor!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: elderly people have crown much experience
q: Much experience is the crown of the aged.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: elderly people have beautiful judgment (in the gray-haired)
q: How beautiful a thing is judgment in the gray-haired, and for elders to know good counsel!

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman is compared to sandy hill (a wife full of words is to a quiet man as a sandy hill is to the aged)
q: As walking up a sandy hill is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman has malice greater than all other malice
q: All malice is small compared to the malice of a woman.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman is origin of sin (the beginning of sin came from a woman)
q: The beginning of sin came from a woman. Because of her, we all die.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman is a abasement of heart (also sadness of countenance and a wounded heart)
q: A wicked woman is abasement of heart, sadness of countenance, and a wounded heart.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman should not be given freedom of speech (instruction)
q: Don’t give water an outlet, and don’t give a wicked woman freedom of speech.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: husband (of the wicked woman) sighs bitterly (when he hears it among his neighbors)
q: Her husband will sit among his neighbors, and when he hears it, he sighs bitterly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: husband (of the wicked woman) is like hands that hang down and weak knees (a woman who won't make her husband happy)
q: A woman who won’t make her husband happy is like hands that hang down, and weak knees.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fear of the Lord surpasses all things
q: The fear of the Lord surpasses all things.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife gives joy to her husband (faithful wife)
q: A faithful wife gives joy to her husband.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman is like chafing yoke
q: A wicked woman is like a chafing yoke.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wicked woman is like to grasp scorpion (for him who takes hold of her)
q: He who takes hold of her is like one who grasps a scorpion.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife is a great gift
q: A good wife is a great gift.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife is given to those who fear the Lord
q: She will be given to those who fear the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife has beauty like the sun rising in the highest places of the Lord (in her well-organized home)
q: As the sun when it arises in the highest places of the Lord, so is the beauty of a good wife in her well-organized home.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife has grace that delights her husband
q: The grace of a wife will delight her husband.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: good wife has knowledge that strengthens her husband's bones
q: Her knowledge will strengthen his bones.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: husband is happy (husband of a good wife)
q: Happy is the husband of a good wife.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: husband has days doubled (husband of a good wife)
q: The number of his days will be doubled.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: husband fulfills years in peace (with a faithful wife)
q: He will fulfill his years in peace.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sin thrusts itself between buying and selling (compared to a nail sticking between stones)
q: As a nail will stick fast between the joinings of stones, so sin will thrust itself in between buying and selling.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: one who reveals secrets cannot find close friend
q: He who reveals secrets destroys trust, and will not find a close friend.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: one who reveals secrets is without hope (unlike a wound or abuse, which can be reconciled)
q: but he who reveals secrets is without hope.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: one who reveals secrets destroys friend (the friendship with a neighbor)
q: for as a man has destroyed his enemy, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: deceitful schemer contrives evil things (winks the eye)
q: One who winks the eye contrives evil things; and those who know him will keep their distance.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: deceitful schemer is avoided by those who know him
q: One who winks the eye contrives evil things; and those who know him will keep their distance.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: deceitful schemer is hated by the Lord
q: I have hated many things, but nothing like him. The Lord will hate him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: evildoers suffer their evil rolling back upon them (they do not know its source)
q: He who does evil things, they will roll back upon him, and he will not know where they came from.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: evildoers fall into their own pit (he who digs a pit)
q: He who digs a pit will fall into it. He who sets a snare will be caught in it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord hates deceitful schemer
q: The Lord will hate him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sin lies in wait for evildoers (compared to a lion lying in wait for prey)
q: The lion lies in wait for prey. So does sin for those who do evil.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: thoughts is test of a person (compared to a furnace testing the potter's vessels)
q: The furnace tests the potter’s vessels; so the test of a person is in his thoughts.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fools has discourse that changes like the moon
q: The discourse of a godly man is always wise, but the fool changes like the moon.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fools has talk that is offensive
q: The talk of fools is offensive.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fools has laughter that is wantonly sinful
q: Their laughter is wantonly sinful.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: fools has talk marked by much swearing (makes hair stand upright)
q: Their talk with much swearing makes hair stand upright.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: one who reveals secrets destroys trust
q: He who reveals secrets destroys trust, and will not find a close friend.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: vengeful man receives vengeance (from the Lord)
q: He who takes vengeance will find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely make his sins firm.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: whisperer is described as double-tongued
q: Curse the whisperer and double-tongued, for he has destroyed many who were at peace.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: whisperer destroys people at peace (many)
q: for he has destroyed many who were at peace.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: whisperer is a slanderer
q: A slanderer has shaken many, and dispersed them from nation to nation.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: whisperer overthrows strong cities (as slanderer)
q: It has pulled down strong cities and overthrown the houses of great men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: whisperer casts out brave women (as slanderer)
q: A slanderer has cast out brave women and deprived them of their labors.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: tongue has stroke that breaks bones
q: the stroke of a tongue will break bones.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: tongue kills more than sword (fallen because of the tongue outnumber those by the sword)
q: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, yet not so many as those who have fallen because of the tongue.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: tongue has yoke made of iron
q: For its yoke is a yoke of iron, and its bands are bands of brass.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: tongue has bands made of brass
q: For its yoke is a yoke of iron, and its bands are bands of brass.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: tongue has death that is evil (worse than Hades)
q: Its death is an evil death, and Hades is better than it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord takes vengeance on vengeful man
q: He who takes vengeance will find vengeance from the Lord

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: tongue has no rule over godly men
q: It will not have rule over godly men.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: tongue falls upon those who forsake the Lord (burns among them unquenched)
q: Those who forsake the Lord will fall into it. It will burn among them, and won’t be quenched.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: vengeful man has effect on sins makes them firm
q: he will surely make his sins firm.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: forgiveness leads to pardon of sins (when one prays)
q: Forgive your neighbor the hurt that he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: anger and wrath is nourished by flesh (man as flesh)
q: He himself, being flesh, nourishes wrath.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: vengeful man shows mercy to none (toward a man like himself)
q: Upon a man like himself he has no mercy

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: strife is kindled by passionate man
q: a passionate man will kindle strife.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: strife effect of abstaining diminishes sins
q: Abstain from strife, and you will diminish your sins

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: strife burns in proportion to its stoutness
q: as the stoutness of the strife is, so it will burn.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: neighbor receives loan (in time of his need)
q: Lend to your neighbor in time of his need.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: almsgiving delivers from affliction (when stored up in store-chambers)
q: Store up almsgiving in your store-chambers and it will deliver you out of all affliction.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: almsgiving fights against enemy (better than a mighty shield and a ponderous spear)
q: It will fight for you against your enemy better than a mighty shield and a ponderous spear.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: guarantor is characterized as good man (one who is surety for his neighbor)
q: A good man will be surety for his neighbor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: guarantor gives his life (for the one he guarantees)
q: Don’t forget the kindness of your guarantor, for he has given his life for you.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: guarantor has property wasted by sinner
q: A sinner will waste the property of his guarantor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: suretyship causes ruin of prosperous people (shakes them like a wave of the sea)
q: Being surety has undone many who were prospering and shaken them as a wave of the sea.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: suretyship drives out mighty men (from their homes, wandering among foreign nations)
q: It has driven mighty men from their homes. They wandered among foreign nations.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: suretyship leads to lawsuits (for a sinner who undertakes contracts for work)
q: A sinner who falls into suretiship and undertakes contracts for work will fall into lawsuits.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sojourner endures miserable life (going from house to house, not daring to open his mouth as a guest)
q: It is a miserable life to go from house to house. Where you are a guest, you dare not open your mouth.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sojourner is commanded by host (to set a table and feed the host, or to leave when an honored guest arrives)
q: “Come here, you sojourner, set a table, and if you have anything in your hand, feed me with it.”

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: creditor lends to neighbor (one who shows mercy)
q: He who shows mercy will lend to his neighbor.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: host gives bitter words (to the guest who entertains and serves, with no thanks)
q: You will entertain, serve drinks, and have no thanks. In addition to this, you will hear bitter words.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: hospitality is grievous to man of understanding (scolding about lodging and insults of creditors)
q: These things are grievous to a man of understanding: The scolding about lodging and the insults of creditors.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: borrower (the one who receives a loan) has disposition submissive before receiving (speaks submissively and kisses hands until he has received)
q: Until he has received, he will kiss a man’s hands. For his neighbor’s money he will speak submissively.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: borrower (the one who receives a loan) has habit delays repayment (prolongs the time, returns excuses, complains about the season)
q: Then when payment is due, he will prolong the time, return excuses, and complain about the season.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: borrower (the one who receives a loan) makes of creditor enemy (when he does not repay, without cause)
q: If not, he has deprived him of his money, and he has gotten him for an enemy without cause.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: loan is considered by many windfall
q: Many have considered a loan to be a windfall, and have given trouble to those who helped them.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: creditor receives from unfaithful borrower half of the loan (if the borrower prevails, hardly even half)
q: If he prevails, the creditor will hardly receive half; and he will count it as a windfall.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man should receive help (for the commandment's sake, according to his need)
q: Help a poor man for the commandment’s sake. According to his need don’t send him empty away.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: poor man should receive patience (his alms should not be delayed)
q: However be patient with a man in poor estate. Don’t keep him waiting for your alms.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: discipline and chastisement of children yields joy (for the father, in the end)
q: He who loves his son will continue to lay stripes upon him, that he may have joy from him in the end.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sorrow has no profit (has destroyed many)
q: for sorrow has destroyed many, and there is no profit in it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: sorrow is to be avoided (removed far from oneself)
q: Remove sorrow far from you

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gladness and cheerfulness is life of a man
q: Gladness of heart is the life of a man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: gladness and cheerfulness lengthens days (of a man)
q: Cheerfulness of a man lengthens his days.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: discipline and chastisement of children yields profit (for the father, from the son)
q: He who chastises his son will have profit from him, and will brag about him among his acquaintances.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: son is like father (when well taught, he is left behind as a likeness)
q: for he has left one behind him like himself.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: son is to be avenger against enemies (when well taught)
q: He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one to repay kindness to his friends.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: son is to be repayer of kindness to friends (when well taught)
q: He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one to repay kindness to his friends.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: son becomes headstrong (when unrestrained)
q: An unrestrained son becomes headstrong.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: discipline and chastisement of children prevents stubbornness (bowing the neck and beating in youth)
q: Bow down his neck in his youth, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he become stubborn, and be disobedient to you, and there be sorrow to your soul.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: health is better than wealth
q: Health and fitness are better than all gold, and a strong body better than wealth without measure.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord honors father (over the children)
q: For the Lord honors the father over the children, and has confirmed the judgment of the mother over her sons.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honoring parents is like laying up treasure (giving glory to mother)
q: He who gives glory to his mother is as one who lays up treasure.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: father has attribute blessing establishes children's houses
q: For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: mother has attribute curse roots out foundations
q: but the curse of the mother roots out the foundations.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: father source of man's glory (through the honor given him)
q: For the glory of a man is from the honor of his father

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: humility results in favor before the Lord
q: The greater you are, humble yourself the more, and you will find favor before the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: humility results in being loved by an acceptable man (going on with business in humility)
q: My son, go on with your business in humility; so you will be loved by an acceptable man.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: pride and stubbornness results in bad end (stubborn heart)
q: A stubborn heart will do badly at the end.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: pride and stubbornness results in burdened with troubles (stubborn heart)
q: A stubborn heart will be burdened with troubles.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: pride and stubbornness has attribute incurable calamity (proud)
q: The calamity of the proud has no healing, for a weed of wickedness has taken root in him.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: pride and stubbornness leads astray many (conceit)
q: For the conceit of many has led them astray.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord confirms mother (judgment over her sons)
q: For the Lord honors the father over the children, and has confirmed the judgment of the mother over her sons.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord has attribute great power
q: For the power of the Lord is great, and he is glorified by those who are lowly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord is glorified by humility (those who are lowly)
q: For the power of the Lord is great, and he is glorified by those who are lowly.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: the Lord curses mother (whoever provokes his mother)
q: He who provokes his mother is cursed by the Lord.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honoring parents results in atonement for sins (honoring father)
q: He who honors his father will make atonement for sins.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honoring parents results in length of days (giving glory to father)
q: He who gives glory to his father will have length of days.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honoring parents results in joy in own children (honoring father)
q: Whoever honors his father will have joy in his own children.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: honoring parents results in answered prayer (honoring father)
q: He will be heard in the day of his prayer.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: riches causes consumed flesh (through wakefulness)
q: Wakefulness that comes from riches consumes the flesh, and anxiety about it takes away sleep.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: table manners and moderate eating requires being first to stop (for manners' sake)
q: Be first to stop for manners’ sake.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: table manners and moderate eating is sufficient with very little food (for a well-mannered man)
q: How sufficient to a well-mannered man is a very little.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wine is good for men life (if drunk in moderation)
q: Wine is as good as life to men, if you drink it in moderation.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wine is created for gladdening men
q: It has been created to make men glad.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wine is joy of heart and gladness of soul (drunk in season and moderation)
q: Wine drunk in season and in moderation is joy of heart and gladness of soul:

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wine is bitterness of soul (drunk excessively)
q: Wine drunk excessively is bitterness of soul, with provocation and conflict.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: wine tests hearts (in quarreling of the proud)
q: so does wine test hearts in the quarreling of the proud.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: riches is a stumbling block (for those who sacrifice to gold)
q: It is a stumbling block to those who sacrifice to it.

l: The Wisdom of Jesus the Son of Sirach, or Ecclesiasticus
s: rich man (the rich person) toils in gathering money
q: A rich man toils in gathering money together.
